images.caption: Avenue of Beeches, Edge of Ken Hill Woods. This is a public right of way along the edge of Ken Hill Woods near Snettisham. The view from here to the west, (Left in the picture) is over fields and water meadows. The sea is not far away! In the woods to the right is the remnants of an ancient tower.

description: This walk explores Wild Ken Hill on the Edge of The Wash in Norfolk. The walk begins in Snettisham and heads west to the coast at Heacham Harbour. The area includes various habitats including grassland, meadow, heathland and shrub. In the middle of the farm, arable farming and intensive grazing have been replaced with low density herbivores (Red Poll cattle, Tamworth pigs, Exmoor ponies). European beavers have been reintroduced within an enclosure.The farm also manages freshwater marsh, river valleys and woodland in a traditional manner in the west of the farm. Part of the route follows theElizabeth Waywhich you can use to extend the walk.
